headline: VRR SURGES 230%: NEVADA MONSTER HOLE — 317m @ 0.77% CuEq From Surface at New Boston Porphyry-Skarn
snippet: VR Resources Limited (TSX-V: VRR) reported an 881m drill hole returning 317 metres of 0.77% copper equivalent starting from surface — including a separate 419m of 0.48% CuEq below 460m — at its New Boston moly-copper-tungsten-silver-zinc porphyry-skarn system in west-central Nevada. The stock surged over 230% on the announcement, the best single-day move in company history, as the intercept confirms extensive continuous polymetallic stockwork veining across a newly identified porphyry target adjacent to Highway 95.

headline: BOSS ENERGY FY26: RECORD 1.41MLB URANIUM, AUD$207M CASH — New Honeymoon Feasibility Study Confirms Expansion Path
snippet: Boss Energy (ASX: BOE) reported FY2026 uranium production of 1.41 million pounds at its Honeymoon mine in South Australia — up 61% from FY2025, with June-quarter output surging 79% quarter-on-quarter to 362,000 pounds. The company closed the year with AUD$207.3 million in cash and zero debt, simultaneously releasing a new feasibility study outlining an expanded capacity pathway at Honeymoon as the global uranium contracting cycle accelerates.

headline: DINOSAURS GROUND KAZATOMPROM — Fossil Find Halts Acid Plant Build; U3O8 Spot Jumps to $89.50/lb, 6-Month High
snippet: Kazakhstan's TQZ sulphuric acid plant — critical to Kazatomprom's uranium leaching capacity — has been suspended after construction crews unearthed potential palaeontological specimens, triggering a legal hold under Kazakh national heritage law. Commissioning is now pushed to Q3 2027–Q1 2028, a 6-to-12-month delay from the original Q1 2027 target; the supply surprise sent U3O8 spot up 4.7% over two weeks to $89.50/lb, its highest level since February 2026.

headline: PALADIN FY26 REVENUE SURGES 71% TO $304M — Langer Heinrich Hits Upper Guidance at 4.82Mlb U₃O₈
snippet: Paladin Energy (ASX: PDN) reported FY2026 sales revenue of US$304.3 million — a 71% year-on-year surge — driven by 4.35 million pounds of uranium sold at an average realised price of US$70.00/lb. Production at Langer Heinrich Mine in Namibia came in at 4.82 million pounds, hitting the upper end of guidance, with cost of production maintained at US$43.3/lb at the lower end of the range, confirming the operation's full-capacity recovery from its 2024 restart.

headline: NEVGOLD 20,000m PROGRAM OPENS HOT — First 3 Holes Push Nevada Antimony-Gold Resource 100m Beyond Its Own Boundaries
snippet: NevGold Corp.'s first three holes of its 2026 20,000-metre drill campaign at Limousine Butte in Nevada have intercepted antimony-gold mineralisation over 100 metres outside the current resource block model, with the best hole returning 1.16% antimony over 3.0 metres within 1.38 g/t gold-equivalent over 50.3 metres from surface. With 25 of 28 completed holes still awaiting assay, the bulk of this year's results remain ahead — and grades in these early holes exceed the current resource average, suggesting a meaningful resource upgrade is coming.

headline: SILVER ADDS 1.7% TO $70.41 FRIDAY — AI Data Centers Join Solar as Structural Industrial Driver; 6th Straight Supply Deficit Looms
snippet: Silver spot rose 1.68% to $70.41 on Friday August 28 as fresh analysis highlights AI infrastructure and data-centre cooling systems emerging as a growing structural silver consumer alongside solar manufacturing. Despite per-panel silver intensity declining 7% this year due to thrifting by solar manufacturers, AI server demand is thrifting-resistant and adds an uncapped new demand layer — while the market heads toward its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit with no meaningful new primary silver mine supply in the pipeline.

headline: NV GOLD TOPS TSX-V WITH 88% WEEKLY GAIN — 2026 Drill Launches at Slumber Gold 60 Miles West of Winnemucca, Nevada
snippet: NV Gold Corporation (TSX-V: NVX) was the week's top performer on the TSX Venture Exchange, surging 88% after announcing the commencement of its 2026 drill program at the Slumber Gold Project in Humboldt County, Nevada. The program targets newly acquired private land that potentially bridges two historically drilled target zones; initial holes will reach depths beyond 300 metres — timed to gold's strongest price environment in decades above $4,600/oz, where even small Nevada gold systems command outsized junior market attention.
